(1) soft clustering and hierarchical clustering are effective in organizing large, heterogeneous collections of law firm documents; (2) soft clustering and/or hierarchical clustering can assist in the generation of legal taxonomies; (3) soft clustering and/ or hierarchical clustering can assist legal researchers by providing an effective alternative to search.
soft clustering techniques are effective in the absence of labeled training data, and that the resulting clusters are of high internal quality and useful in the generation of taxonomies.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a set of tools that can help lawyers and law firms manage their electronic work product in a distributed and efficient manner.
exploring and evaluating the use of document clustering as a tool for legal research and knowledge management.
the application of clustering to large heterogeneous law firm data collections and the development of a set of effective and efficient clustering tools.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
document clustering is a viable approach to knowledge management for large heterogeneous law firms, especially when a relevant legal taxonomy does not exist.
soft and hierarchical clustering techniques are more effective than traditional hard clustering for the task of document clustering.
soft clustering and hierarchical clustering can be used as effective alternatives to traditional clustering in the absence of a legal taxonomy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
clustering is an effective and useful tool for organizing large heterogeneous collections of law firm documents, and that soft clustering is a promising technique for this purpose.
clustering can provide an efficient and effective method for the analysis of large heterogeneous law firm document collections.
soft clustering techniques, in conjunction with hierarchical clustering and a number of additional enhancements, are effective for document clustering in the legal domain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
clustering is a useful tool for organizing large, heterogeneous collections, and can be used as a precursor to classification.
soft hierarchical clustering, when applied in a legal context, can be used to organize large document collections, and can be a powerful tool for knowledge management.
soft and hierarchical clustering techniques are effective and efficient for large heterogeneous collections, such as those found in law firms, where no a priori taxonomy exists.
